title: Workflows and agents: who owns the control flow

items.stem: In a workflow, what decides the order of the steps?

options.text: The model chooses each next step while it runs
Code that the developer wrote sets the steps ahead of time
The student picks each next step during the chat
The tool descriptions fix the order of the steps

items.stem: Your code always runs check_calendar first, then calls the model once to write the answer. Is this a workflow or an agent?
Booking a machine always needs the same three steps in the same order: check the calendar, check the training record, then book. Which design fits best?

options.text: An agent that picks the tools and their order each time
Three agents, one for each step, that work together
A fixed workflow that runs the three steps in that order
An agent with a larger context window to hold more

items.stem: Why does a fixed workflow often cost less per request than an agent doing the same task?

options.text: Code sets the steps, so no model calls choose them
Workflows skip tools, so no tool results enter context
Workflows never call a model, so they use no tokens
Workflows reuse answers from earlier students' requests

items.stem: Which request needs an agent more than a fixed workflow?

options.text: Send the same reminder to every student with a booking
Show the opening hours of the 3D printer room
Reformat a booking time from 24-hour to 12-hour
Find a free slot for a vague plan on any machine

items.stem: A workflow makes exactly 2 model calls per request. An agent makes 5 on average. For 100 requests, how many more model calls does the agent make?
